RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 65

An all-male panel selecting a candidate with notably less leadership background (informal courses and teaching experience versus your Master’s degree and five years as deputy principal) is a red flag for implicit or affinity bias. The delayed written explanation adds procedural concern. 

However, whether to raise gender bias depends on your jurisdiction, union backing, and career goals. Leveling accusations prematurely can trigger defensiveness and close doors. Instead, follow up firmly on your written feedback request, ideally through a union representative or employment advisor. If the provided rationale fails to objectively justify choosing a candidate with significantly fewer formal leadership credentials, you will have a much stronger basis to challenge the decision.
